title: Recurrent pressure rise
openingNarrative: Ventilator pressures are climbing again. Right-sided air entry is reduced. The tracheostomy tube is patent—ordinary suction retrieves little secretion. Rohan uses auditory scanning to report RIGHT MIDDLE. A simplified overlay shows a possible distal plug. The clinician explains uncertainty at eye level. No family member answers on his behalf. Three imperfect options appear before any outcome is revealed.
clinicalState: Rising peak pressures. Reduced right-sided air entry. Patent tracheostomy with little suction yield. Differential includes distal mucus plug, focal atelectasis, secretion burden, inflammation; pneumothorax is not diagnosed without supporting findings. Severe cardiomyopathy with ICD in situ; cardiac reserve limited—aggressive recruitment has previously linked to ventricular instability and ICD therapy.

choices.label: Early planned bronchoscopy through the tracheostomy
choices.immediateConsequence: Team prepares controlled bronchoscopy without graphic procedural display. Procedural and cardiac risk rise; obstruction may be confirmed or cleared.
choices.delayedConsequence: Branch A consequence follows: plug removal may coincide with brief hypotension without arrest. Access must stay available through the procedure window.
choices.rohanAacLine: THE LAST EMERGENCY IS HISTORY. CHECK WHAT THIS ONE IS.

choices.label: Targeted humidification, positioning, and cautious clearance with observation
choices.immediateConsequence: Pressures may ease partially without a scope. Obstruction certainty remains low; observation burden rises.
choices.delayedConsequence: Branch B consequence follows: partial improvement can mask a plug that later worsens. Not framed as the gentle correct answer—only a different risk profile.
choices.rohanAacLine: NOT EVERY ALARM IS A CODE.

choices.label: More aggressive pressure recruitment to re-expand the right lung
choices.immediateConsequence: Aeration may improve briefly. Cardiac and lung-injury risk climb because high-pressure techniques have previously triggered ventricular instability.
choices.delayedConsequence: Branch C consequence follows: brief gain can trade into arrhythmia burden and concern for pressure-related lung injury.
choices.rohanAacLine: EVERY ALARM STILL DESERVES AN ANSWER.

disabilityRightsNotes: Rohan reports the symptom location; staff do not speak over him.
Bronchoscopy is a decision, not an automatic ritual.
Camera stays at or below Rohan’s eye level when he is addressed.
debriefNotes: Prompt 7 decision beat: three airway strategies, outcome not yet revealed.
Patent tracheostomy with distal obstruction is clinically coherent.
No correct-answer language in the node or media.
Instrumental Action Stations (assets 01–20) investigate Airway, Breathing+Equipment, and Circulation before pathway commit — equipment available is not action indicated.
